summary: The shipped FlowDefinition's own header prescribes an operator sequence the request door refuses. It states a `disposition` step's `evidenceRefs`/`targetRef` "may cite `human-turn:<turnId>` today" and makes that step (1) of "the intended sequence a driver follows". Empirically false: the charset check rejects it. The same paragraph also mis-attributes the avoidance of `grantedContextRefs` to that channel being "unchecked", when it is in fact charset-refused too. The conformance test (lines 328-339) and doer-report.md both state the correct thing -- only the YAML, the artifact Phase 04's skill authors will read, was never updated after the gap was found.
evidence:
Live probe against the real `validateCoordinationRequest` (src/verbs/coordination/schema.mjs), declared-protocol request bound to this protocol:
  ACCEPTED :: disposition, evidenceRefs=['a1']            (control)
  REFUSED  :: disposition, evidenceRefs=['human-turn:t1'] -> steps[0].evidenceRefs[0] "human-turn:t1" contains characters outside the safe filesystem charset (letters, digits, underscore, hyphen only) -- path escape rejected
  REFUSED  :: disposition, targetRef='human-turn:t1'      -> same charset error
  REFUSED  :: disposition, evidenceRefs=['contribution:c1'] -> same charset error
  REFUSED  :: authorize, grantedContextRefs=['human-turn:t1'] -> same charset error
Root cause: SAFE_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/ (schema.mjs:29), applied by assertSafeRefOrId (schema.mjs:77-88) at schema.mjs:337 (grantedContextRefs), :363 (disposition.targetRef), :374 (disposition.evidenceRefs). No colon is admitted, so BOTH reserved namespaces are refused, for EVERY protocol, in every ref field. The doer's disclosed gap is accurate and if anything understated by the YAML.
recommendation: Correct the YAML header paragraph to match the code and the doer report: a `disposition` step naming a `human-turn:` ref is refused at the request-schema charset check for all protocols, so the only channel available today through `fgos coordination run --file`/the pack gate is the `authorize` step's free-text `reason`. Delete or rewrite the "(1) `disposition` step citing `human-turn:<turnId>` as `evidenceRefs`" instruction, and replace "since that channel is unchecked" with the real reason. Prose-only edit; no code or test change.

summary: `revise-explanation` -- a declared operation with a `driver-authorized`, `activation.maxInvocations: 2` binding, and half of the "bounded dialogue reopen" capability phase-03 requires -- has zero test coverage. It could be deleted from the FlowDefinition entirely and all 12 conformance tests would still pass. This is the one genuine phantom-shaped guarantee in the cell: a declared bound capability with nothing asserting it.
evidence: `grep -rn "revise-explanation" test/` returns zero matches; `grep -c` in the conformance file returns 0. Deletion is provably test-neutral: the binding is `driver-authorized` with NO `contextAccess.visibilityWindowRef`, so per `actorGatingOperationIds` (session-engine.mjs:1362-1379) it is deliberately EXCLUDED from lead-advisor-actor's quorum-gating set and cannot affect any `closed`/`quorum` assertion; it appears in no visibility window's `opensAfter`/`permits` and in no specialist slot, so it is inert to every other derivation. Only `revise-synthesis` is exercised (full-chain test call 6; over-cap test calls 4/5/6), and so only `revise-synthesis`'s own maxInvocations:2 cap is proven.
recommendation: Add a conformance case that authorizes and dispatches `revise-explanation` after a human turn and asserts (a) a genuinely new Assignment distinct from the original `explain-recommendation`, and (b) its own N+1 refusal at the third authorization, mirroring the existing `revise-synthesis` over-cap test. Alternatively, if lead-advisor reopen is not actually wanted in V1, drop the operation and binding rather than shipping an unproven one.

summary: Two rejection predicates assert only the error CLASS, with no message discrimination -- the only two in a file that otherwise uses a specific regex for every refusal. The specialist case is the weaker of the two: its negative arm omits BOTH the slot authorization and the operation authorization, so it does not isolate the guarantee its own name claims ("cannot dispatch without a prior authorizeSpecialistSlot").
evidence:
Line 566: `(err) => err instanceof CoordinationError` for the unauthorized-specialist dispatch. Line 857: `(err) => err instanceof CoordinationError` for `recordDriverDisposition` with a never-recorded `human-turn:` ref. Contrast every sibling assertion in the same file, which pins the message: /visibility window "post-shaping-open" to be open/ (:415), /resolves to an Assignment that is not a member of coordination session/ (:470), /visibility window "post-critique-open" to be open/ (:501), /maxInvocations/ (:690), /is not active \(status: "completed"\)/ (:778), /carries Work lifecycle authority/ (:797), /attributedTo\.type must be "person"/ (:837).
The refusal is currently thrown for the right reason -- the unbound-slot check at session-engine.mjs:1040-1044 fires during actor resolution, ahead of the driver-authorization check -- so this is a loss of test POWER, not a live defect. But because the negative arm supplies neither authorization, the test cannot distinguish "slot not authorized" from "operation not authorized", and would keep passing if the slot gate were removed and the generic authorization gate caught it instead.
recommendation: Pin both predicates to their real messages (e.g. /is bound to specialist slot "specialist-answer-slot" -- no specialist is currently authorized/ and the store door's own never-recorded-turn message). For the specialist case, additionally authorize the OPERATION but not the SLOT in the negative arm, so the refusal can only come from the slot gate.

summary: Phase-03's Tests First list names "foreign/stale refs"; only the foreign half is tested. The file's own section header says "Foreign/stale refs are refused" but contains a single test, for a cross-session Assignment ref. No case covers a stale ref -- a superseded revision, or an artifact edited since settle (which `linkSessionContribution` refuses under a revision-pin mismatch).
evidence: `grep -i "stale"` in the conformance file matches only the section-header comment at line 437. The foreign-ref test itself is strong (real second session on the same .fgos root, specific message pattern, zero-new-events assertion, and the foreign ref smuggled alongside a genuinely owned one).
recommendation: Add a stale-ref case: settle a contribution, mutate the backing artifact on disk, and assert the revision-pin refusal -- or record explicitly in the P03.2 report that "stale" is judged already covered by the kernel-level contribution suite and out of this protocol's own conformance scope.

summary: "Wrong recheck revision" (also from phase-03's Tests First list) is proven only as an immutability property -- that three distinct synthesizer Assignments coexist -- not as a refusal. Nothing asserts that a recheck citing a wrong or superseded revision is rejected.
evidence: The single assertion carrying the phrase is `assert.deepEqual(synthesizerAssignmentIds, new Set([synthId, revise1Id, revise2Id]), 'wrong recheck revision: exactly three distinct Assignments, original preserved alongside both reopens')`. That genuinely proves append-only, non-superseding reopen (a real requirement, well covered), but it is a different property from refusing a wrong-revision recheck.
recommendation: Either add a refusal case, or retitle the assertion to what it actually proves ("original evidence is immutable across bounded reopens") and state in the report that the wrong-revision refusal is a kernel-level guarantee proven elsewhere, so the phase checklist is not silently marked satisfied by a differently-shaped proof.

summary: Phase-03 item 2 asks for "the artifact envelope/templates at the existing registry path selected by P02.1". The cell reduces this to `task.contractTemplate` string ids that resolve to nothing anywhere in the codebase. This is defensible -- P02.1 never actually selected a registry path, and every sibling protocol uses contractTemplate the same inert way -- but it should be named as a deliverable satisfied nominally rather than treated as closed.
evidence: The only validation is `if (!isNonEmptyString(op.task.contractTemplate)) fail(...)` -- a non-empty string check, no registry lookup, no file resolution. `grep -rn contractTemplate src/` returns exactly those three lines plus the field whitelist at :85. Sibling protocols (declared-consult, deliberation-{delphi,nominal-group,rfc}-chain, group-cognition-framework) all use bare ids the same way, so this is consistent reuse rather than novel drift. Independently checked P02.1 in full: it contains no row selecting an artifact-envelope registry path, so there was nothing for this cell to build against. The substantive half of the requirement ("enforce identity, type, provenance, source refs, and revision where safety/replay needs them") IS genuinely met by kernel reuse -- `linkSessionContribution` pins artifactRef + a revision hash of the classified bytes and refuses an artifact edited since settle.
recommendation: No code change. Record in the P03.2 report that phase-03 item 2 was satisfied by reusing an existing, unresolved string field because P02.1 selected no registry, so a later phase does not read "artifact envelope shipped" as meaning a validated template registry exists.

summary: `framing-shaping-open`'s `permits.sourceOperationRefs` lists the three shapers themselves. Read literally, that window declares the shapers may receive each other's artifact refs -- the exact isolation this protocol's own header claims to preserve. Inert today and precedented, but latent if `permits` is ever enforced.
evidence: `permits` is consumed nowhere outside validation: `grep -rn permits src/` returns only src/runner/definitions/schema.mjs (field whitelist + shape validation at :365-380) and unrelated prose in store/cohort-planner/run/iron-law. `deriveVisibilityWindowState` (session-engine.mjs:1643-1657) reads ONLY `window.opensAfter.operationRefs`; `permits` never reaches the open/closed decision or any context assembly. The real, kernel-enforced isolation here is separate and holds: the three shaper bindings are `required`, so they carry no `authorize` step and therefore no `grantedContextRefs` -- nothing is granted to them at all. The shape also byte-matches the precedent the header cites: group-thinking-nominal-group-lite.yaml's `private-open` (lines 78-84) is the same vacuous window naming its own gated operation as its permitted source.
recommendation: No change required. Optionally narrow `permits.sourceOperationRefs` to `[]` for this window, since the header already explains it exists only to give the shapers' contributions a window to be legal under -- an empty source list expresses that intent without declaring a reveal the protocol does not want.

summary: The missing `specialist-authorize` request-step type is confirmed exactly as disclosed. Worth stating its consequence plainly: "specialists", one of the seven capabilities phase-03 requires the graph to support, ships graph-declared but not operable through `fgos coordination run --file`/the pack gate -- only via a direct `authorizeSpecialistSlot` engine call.
evidence: The step dispatcher admits exactly six types -- operation, fan-out, authorize, disposition, contribution, human-turn -- and its own failure message enumerates the same six. No `specialist-authorize` anywhere in src/. The conformance test correctly and openly falls back to direct engine calls for this one case (test lines 532-610), and the gap is disclosed in the YAML header, the test header comment, and doer-report.md. Claim accurate, not overstated.
recommendation: No change in this cell -- correctly out of scope per "no speculative kernel work". Ensure it is carried onto the blocker list for whoever owns run.mjs's step vocabulary, alongside the R1 charset gap, since both block the same door for every protocol rather than just this one.
